reason: The blade is the lamina, so the blade apex is the leaf apex. PO lists 'leaf lamina apex' as a synonym.
'leaf lamina apex' is a PO synonym of leaf apex.
French for the apex of the lamina, which is the leaf apex.
The dorsal sepal is one particular sepal, mostly in orchids. Mapping it to 'sepal' would spread its qualities to all sepals. It needs a position-specific class, or the rule should be dropped.
Same as 'dorsal sepal'. The position (dorsal) is lost.
Inner petals are a distinct whorl or set, for example in Annonaceae. Mapping them to 'petal' loses which petals the quality applies to.

A sac on the lip (labellum) is a pouch, not a spur. A spur is a tubular or conical extension, and a sac is a different structure. The PO 'petal spur' class does not fit, and a labellum with a saccate shape would be a better fit.
Same as 'lip sac'. A sac is not a spur.
Outer petals are a specific set (for example Annonaceae outer versus inner petals). The position is lost.
In grasses the sessile spikelet differs from the pedicelled one. Mapping to 'spikelet' loses that contrast and makes the statement ambiguous.
A staminal sheath is the tube formed by fused filaments (monadelphous), which is the staminal tube.
A stamen sheath is the same structure as the staminal tube.
Endostome processes (segments and cilia) are the inner peristome. Peristome teeth are mainly the exostome. The two are not the same structure.
Spore sac is a common name for sporangium. PO lists 'spore case' and 'spore capsule' as synonyms.
The receptacular tube (floral cup) is the hypanthium.
The axis of the spikelet is the rachilla.
'Parallel vein' describes the venation pattern, which is a quality of the leaf, not a vascular bundle. It should be a leaf vein with a parallel-venation quality.
Same as 'parallel vein'. It is a venation pattern, not the part.
Same as 'parallel vein'. It is a venation pattern, not the part.
The principal nerve is the main (primary) vein or midvein of the leaf. 'Vascular bundle' is far too general. Use primary leaf vein, or leaf midvein PO_0020139 for a single midrib.
The principal vein is the primary leaf vein or midvein, not any vascular bundle.
A root hair is a root hair cell, a single-cell outgrowth.
Plural of 'root hair'.
The seed scar is the hilum, the scar where the seed was attached.
French for 'seed scar', which is the hilum.
Intercostal veins run between the costal (secondary) veins, which makes them tertiary veins in leaf architecture.
Plural of 'intercostal vein'.
Used alone, 'intercostals' also means the intercostal zones or tissue between veins, mainly in grasses. It is not always a vein.
A stipular sheath is a sheath made of fused stipules, which is the ochrea.
A stipular tube is the same as the ochrea.
'present' is a quality (presence) and is lost when only the bearer is mapped. This should be an entity_presence rule on 'colleters'.
'Calycine' says where the colleters are (on the calyx). Plain 'colleter' loses this. It needs a calyx container, or the rule should be dropped.
A misspelling of 'inflorescence'.
A stipitate (stalked) gland is usually a glandular trichome. The generic 'gland' loses the stalk. Check against the glandular trichome class.
Plural of 'stipitate gland'. Same issue.
'aerial root' is a PO synonym of shoot-borne root.
Plural of 'aerial root'.
French for 'aerial root'.
A dichasium is a PO synonym of cyme inflorescence. A dichasial cyme is a cyme.
Plural of 'dichasial cyme'.
'Discoid' (disc-shaped) is a shape of the gland and is lost. The generic secretory tissue class says nothing of the gland type.
Plural of 'discoid gland'. Same issue.
'Perfect' means bisexual, which is a quality of the flower. A stamen is not 'perfect' in that sense. It is not a kind of stamen.
Same as 'perfect stamen'. It describes the flower's sexuality, not a type of stamen.
A stalked gland is a glandular trichome with a stalk. The stalk is lost when mapped to generic gland tissue.
Plural of 'stalked gland'. Same issue.
It is a cyme, but the umbel-like shape is lost. The shape should be kept as a quality.
It is a cyme, but the umbel-like shape is lost. The shape should be kept as a quality.

'present' is a presence quality, not part of the bearer name. A hair-point is an apical hair tip, and it is not the same as the leaf apex. It needs an entity_presence rule on a hair-point, or a hairy-tipped apex.
Umbel rays are the first-order branches of the umbel. PO gives 'first order inflorescence branch' as a synonym of second order inflorescence axis.
